title: Triage of browser console errors on the DCLab notebook: a browser extension, not a bug
request: The owner pasted the browser console of the DCLab notebook: runtime.lastError lines, Grammarly warnings, stack traces that mention saveContract in project.js, and a blocked Open Sans stylesheet.
spec: Say whether any of it is a DCLab bug, where each line comes from, and what to do; change code only if a real defect is found.
plan: Identify which app produced the console: the DCLab notebook served by make notebook, not the demo.
Group the lines by source: the extension's own logging, stack traces passing through the app's code, and the blocked stylesheet.
Search the app's static files for the stylesheet that was blocked.
Read the server's content security policy to see why it was blocked.
Answer in English and Persian, and ask for what visibly went wrong, if anything.

decisions.why: Every line traced back to the browser extension; the app's own behaviour was correct.

decisions.decision: The blocked stylesheet was reported as the security policy working, not as an error.
decisions.why: The notebook never loads Open Sans; the extension tried to inject it, and the policy (style-src 'self') rightly refused it.

decisions.decision: The answer asked for a visible symptom instead of guessing at one.
decisions.why: A noisy console is not a defect; a contract that did not save or a stage that did not unlock would be.

change: None: a diagnosis. The Grammarly lines and runtime.lastError are the extension's logging; saveContract appears in the stack only because the extension attaches to the new text fields when the page re-renders after the contract is saved; the Open Sans request came from the extension and was refused by the app's content security policy. Advice: open the notebook in a private window or turn the extension off for the local address.

findings.defect: Console errors that looked like a failure in the notebook's contract form.
findings.scenario: After saving the prediction contract, the console filled with warnings whose stack traces pass through saveContract in project.js, plus a refused Open Sans stylesheet.
findings.cause: A grammar-checking browser extension that attaches to new text fields and injects its own stylesheet; the app's code was only on the stack.
findings.fix: No code change: explain the source, confirm the security policy refused the injected stylesheet as designed, and suggest a private window or turning the extension off for the local address.
findings.test: A search of dclab_rnd/agentic/static found no Google Fonts or Open Sans reference.
findings.impact: Taken at face value, the console would have led to changes in the contract save code for a defect it did not have, or to a looser content security policy that lets an extension inject resources.
alternatives: Allow the font in the content security policy: set aside because the notebook never loads Open Sans; the extension tried to inject it, and the refusal is the policy working.

outcome: Done: no DCLab defect; the owner was told where each line came from and what would count as a real symptom.
lessons: Before fixing a console error, find which code wrote it; a function on the stack is not always the culprit.
A refusal by the content security policy is often the defence working; check whether the app ever asked for that resource.
risks: Treating a function that appears on a stack trace as the source of the error.
Loosening the content security policy to silence a refused stylesheet the app never asked for.
Changing code with no visible symptom to fix.
